Bootstrap5Renderer::createPageJumpContainer() mutates the HTMLTag $input and $button objects it receives (adds classes and a style attribute) before appending them to the container. The mutation order is correct and the scope is tightly contained within the private createPageJumpInput() call chain, so there is no observable defect. A future-proof alternative would be to have the hook receive only scalar data (e.g., the GridPagination object) and build all elements itself, eliminating the coupling to the caller's object graph.

No improvement — code is clean and consistent on the security surface. json_encode() with JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR is correctly used to escape both the URL template and the input element ID before injection into the inline onclick JavaScript in createPageJumpInput().
